title: Haze on a small moon
paragraphs: The thin atmosphere of a small, cold moon should not be able to hold clouds, yet images show persistent haze over its southern hemisphere. One group of planetary scientists attributes the haze to hydrocarbon particles formed when sunlight breaks apart methane high in the atmosphere. This explanation fits the haze's altitude and color, and laboratory experiments have reproduced similar particles. A second group proposes that the haze consists instead of fine ice crystals lofted by seasonal winds, a hypothesis that, if correct, would predict that the haze thins as the southern summer ends. Observations over the next few years may settle the matter, but for now neither account can be ruled out.
